citation: Kiratipaisarl W, Surawattanasakul V, Sirikul W. Individual and organizational interventions to reduce burnout in resident physicians: a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Medical Education, 2024 (received 11 May 2024, accepted 15 Oct 2024; PMID 39478552; PMCID PMC11523819; doi 10.1186/s12909-024-06195-3). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11523819/ [title wording reconstructed from abstract; not copied from the page header, uncertain]

date_and_recency: Published 2024 (accepted 15 Oct 2024). Abstract gives the search window as '1 December 2023 to 26 August 2024', which looks like an update window; the protocol was registered in 2022 (CRD42022349698). Included studies span roughly 2015 to 2023. [uncertain: exact search window]
key_claims: Individual interventions (coaching, meditation) reduced emotional exhaustion and depersonalization by small amounts versus control. Organizational interventions (work-hour changes, learning-environment changes) showed no significant pooled effect on any MBI domain. Authors judge practical significance as none to small, certainty as very low (GRADE) for every outcome, and recommend combined individual plus organizational approaches in future studies. Subgroup hints: coaching helped EE, meditation helped PA, learning-environment changes helped PA, work-hour changes helped little; interventions longer than 6 months looked better for EE/DP.
headline_figures: Pooled individual interventions vs control, post-intervention Cohen's d: EE -0.25 (95% CI -0.40 to -0.11, I2 49.3%); DP -0.17 in abstract but -0.18 in results text (95% CI -0.32 to -0.03, p=0.02, I2 50.0%); PA 0.18 (95% CI 0.00 to 0.35, p=0.05, I2 57.2%), not significant.
Pooled organizational interventions: EE -0.22 (95% CI -0.47 to 0.04, p=0.10, I2 62.6%); DP -0.15 (-0.38 to 0.08, p=0.21); PA 0.12 (-0.01 to 0.25, p=0.07). None significant.
Meditation subgroup (9 studies): PA 0.22 (95% CI 0.03 to 0.40, p=0.02, I2 0%). EE reported as -0.30 (-0.61 to 0.02, p=0.25) in results text but -0.33 (-0.59 to -0.08) in GRADE table.
Work-hour subgroup (6 studies in text; 5 cited): EE -0.20 (-0.58 to 0.17), DP -0.16, PA 0.04. All non-significant.
Improved-learning-environment subgroup (2 historical-control studies, 161 intervention vs 148 control... as listed): PA 0.28 (0.05 to 0.50); EE and DP non-significant.
Organizational studies lasting 6+ months: EE -0.33 (-0.60 to -0.07), DP -0.28 (-0.48 to -0.08); under 6 months: nothing.

Screening: 1283 records, 496 duplicates removed, 787 screened, 113 full text retrieved, 53 'met the criteria' then 33 eligible. Total n=2536. 25 individual studies (16 coaching, 9 meditation), 8 organizational (6 work-hour, 2 learning environment).
sample_unit_and_population: 33 controlled studies of resident (postgraduate trainee) physicians across specialties, total n=2536 (pooled per-arm counts differ by outcome). Control designs mixed: historical-control, self-control (pre/post), and RCT; the authors say studies were predominantly non-randomized. Not software engineers.
observed_vs_stated: Entirely self-reported. Outcome is Maslach Burnout Inventory scores (22-item, 16-item, 20-item, 9-item abbreviated versions). No blinding. No observed behaviour or physiological measures.
what_it_measures_or_defines: Burnout defined by WHO as an occupational phenomenon from prolonged exposure to psychosocial workplace risk factors, operationalised through the Maslach three-domain model: high emotional exhaustion (EE), high depersonalization (DP), low personal accomplishment (PA). Only studies using the MBI were searched; mixed MBI versions were pooled as standardised mean differences (Cohen's d). Practical significance judged against Cochrane Handbook thresholds.
mechanism_or_cause: Not tested. Introduction cites psychosocial workplace risk factors (WHO) and Maslach framework. Discussion speculates that work-hour mandates reduce residents' autonomy and disrupt shift handovers and continuity of care, while workflow streamlining and food catering disrupt less.
interventions_and_effects: Individual: coaching (positive psychology workshops, resilience, stress management, soft skills; EE -0.24) and meditation or mindfulness (PA +0.22). Organizational: work-hour modification (shift length, hour limits, day of rest after a shift; no significant effect) and improved learning environment (workflow streamlining, healthy snacks, continuous assessment of burnout and learning environments; PA +0.28, only 2 studies). Authors suggest coaching 1 to 2 h/week, 1 to 2 times a month, for 6 to 12 months; evaluation of work-hour changes after 2 to 4 months; learning environment changes over 1 to 2 years. Qualitative synthesis favours bundling individual and organizational approaches. All tested on resident physicians.
transfer_to_software_teams: Weak. Evidence is from physician trainees, not engineers or open source. Residency has distinct features (mandated hours, patient-safety handover, training status). Most useful as a caution: even in a large healthcare literature, interventions show small effects and low-certainty evidence, and the organizational side is under-studied rather than shown ineffective.
limitations_stated: MBI only, other tools excluded; assumed comparability of control and intervention types leading to heterogeneity (I2 up to ~70% in subgroups); population heterogeneity across specialties and cultures; high risk of bias from subjective unblinded outcomes and inadequate confounder control in non-randomized studies; few and varied organizational studies, so possibly underpowered. Participant compliance noted as a critical consideration. Authors report no publication bias from funnel plots (supplement not opened).
counter_evidence: Internal inconsistencies weaken the headline: (1) DP pooled is -0.17 in abstract and -0.18 in results; (2) meditation EE is -0.30 (CI -0.61 to 0.02, p=0.25) in text but -0.33 (CI -0.59 to -0.08) in GRADE table; (3) coaching EE p=0.04 and subgroup p-values do not always match their CIs (e.g. EE -0.22 CI -0.47 to 0.04 p=0.10 plausible, but others odd); (4) the work-hour group has 6 studies in the GRADE table but 5 citations; (5) conclusion states organizational interventions 'resulted in small but significant enhancements in PA' though the pooled organizational PA was non-significant and the claim rests on 2 historical-control studies; (6) a significant PA effect (0.18, p=0.05) is described as non-significant; (7) results say 53 studies 'met the criteria' then 33 eligible, reasons unclear in main text; (8) search window dates in abstract inconsistent with 2022 registration. Subgroup claims (coaching vs meditation) are labelled exploratory. Earlier reviews (Panagioti 2017) found organizational interventions were at least as effective, so this review's null on organizational may reflect power, not absence of effect.
verification_status: Pooled effects, CIs, GRADE rating (very low for all outcomes), study counts and limitations: checked against the PMC full text actually opened. Discrepancies listed above verified by comparing abstract, results text and Table 2. Supplementary appendices, individual trial data and forest plots: not opened [uncertain]. Search date window: [uncertain].
usable_claim: A 2024 meta-analysis of 33 mostly non-randomized studies in resident physicians found that individual interventions such as coaching and meditation reduced self-reported emotional exhaustion by a small amount (d about -0.25), while organizational interventions showed no statistically significant pooled effect. The authors rated the certainty of all outcomes as very low and called for combined individual and organizational approaches. The null organizational result is attributed partly to few, varied studies.
do_not_use: Do not say organizational interventions do not work; the review says underpowered. Do not cite the subgroup 'meditation improves PA' or 'learning environment improves PA' as findings (exploratory, 2 studies for learning environment). Do not quote DP or meditation EE figures without noting the abstract/results/table mismatches. Do not present results as applying to software engineers. Do not use the suggested dose (1 to 2 h/week for 6 to 12 months) as evidence-based.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the essays' text. Unlikely to be used by 'Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part', the trust essay or 'Checking Isn't Catching' (topic is burnout interventions; likely a new source). Panagioti 2017 is a related source already in results/. [uncertain]
